name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q01 - Matching organic acids with producing microbes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Microorganism) List II (Organic Acid)
A. Aspergillus nigerI. Acetic acid
B. Acetobacter acetiII. Lactic acid
C. Clostridium butylicumIII. Citric acid
D. LactobacillusIV. Butyric acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Aspergillus niger
Aspergillus niger is a fungus utilized for the industrial production of citric acid.

Step 2: Role of Acetobacter aceti
Acetobacter aceti is a bacterium responsible for the commercial production of acetic acid.

Step 3: Role of Clostridium butylicum
Clostridium butylicum is a bacterium that ferments substrates to yield butyric acid.

Step 4: Role of Lactobacillus
Lactobacillus is a lactic acid bacterium that converts milk to curd by producing lactic acid and partially digesting milk proteins.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Matching the microorganisms with their respective produced organic acids gives: Aspergillus niger with citric acid, Acetobacter aceti with acetic acid, Clostridium butylicum with butyric acid, and Lactobacillus with lactic acid. Hence, the correct combination is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q02 - Matching household food items with responsible microbes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Organism / Process) List II (Product / Feature)
A. Saccharomyces cerevisiaeI. Large holes in Swiss cheese
B. Propionibacterium sharmaniII. Traditional drink 'Toddy'
C. Lactic acid bacteriaIII. Fermentation of bread dough
D. Fermentation of palm sapIV. Curd formation with vitamin B12 enrichment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used for the fermentation of bread dough, where carbon dioxide production gives the dough its puffed-up appearance.

Step 2: Role of Propionibacterium sharmani
The bacterium Propionibacterium sharmani produces large amounts of carbon dioxide, which creates the large holes characteristic of Swiss cheese.

Step 3: Role of Lactic acid bacteria
Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) grow in milk and convert it into curd by producing acids that coagulate milk proteins, simultaneously enhancing nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B12.

Step 4: Role of palm sap fermentation
'Toddy' is a traditional drink of parts of southern India prepared by fermenting the sap collected from palms.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Aligning each microbial agent or process with its corresponding product yields: Saccharomyces cerevisiae with bread dough fermentation, Propionibacterium sharmani with Swiss cheese holes, Lactic acid bacteria with curd formation and vitamin B12 enrichment, and palm sap fermentation with the traditional beverage Toddy. Thus, the correct sequence is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q03 - Matching bioactive molecules with their therapeutic applications

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Bioactive Molecule / Enzyme) List II (Function / Application)
A. StreptokinaseI. Immunosuppressive agent in organ transplants
B. Cyclosporin AII. Clot buster for clearing intravascular thrombi
C. StatinsIII. Detergent additive for removing oily stains
D. LipasesIV. Competitive inhibitor of cholesterol synthesis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Streptokinase
Streptokinase, produced by Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering, functions as a clot buster for clearing thrombi from blood vessels of patients who have suffered myocardial infarction.

Step 2: Role of Cyclosporin A
Cyclosporin A, extracted from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum, is clinically administered as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients.

Step 3: Role of Statins
Statins, synthesized by the yeast Monascus purpureus, act as blood-cholesterol lowering agents by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis.

Step 4: Role of Lipases
Lipases are lipid-digesting enzymes used in laundry detergent formulations to remove oily and greasy stains.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Pairing each substance with its medical or commercial role gives: Streptokinase with clot buster action, Cyclosporin A with immunosuppression in organ transplants, Statins with competitive inhibition of cholesterol synthesis, and Lipases with oil stain removal in detergents. Hence, the correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q04 - Matching microbial sources with commercial chemical products

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Microorganism) List II (Bioactive Molecule / Product)
A. Trichoderma polysporumI. Streptokinase
B. Monascus purpureusII. Statins
C. StreptococcusIII. Cyclosporin A
D. Aspergillus nigerIV. Citric acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Product from Trichoderma polysporum
The fungus Trichoderma polysporum is the commercial biological source of the immunosuppressive agent Cyclosporin A.

Step 2: Product from Monascus purpureus
The yeast Monascus purpureus produces statins, which are utilized as blood-cholesterol lowering agents.

Step 3: Product from Streptococcus
The bacterium Streptococcus yields the clot buster enzyme streptokinase, which is subsequently modified via genetic engineering.

Step 4: Product from Aspergillus niger
The fungus Aspergillus niger is grown industrially for the large-scale production of citric acid.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Connecting each microorganism to its bioactive molecule or chemical product gives: Trichoderma polysporum produces Cyclosporin A, Monascus purpureus produces Statins, Streptococcus produces Streptokinase, and Aspergillus niger produces Citric acid. Thus, the correct sequence is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q05 - Matching biocontrol agents with their target pests

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Biocontrol Agent) List II (Target / Application Scope)
A. Ladybird beetleI. Mosquitoes
B. DragonfliesII. Species-specific narrow-spectrum insecticidal applications
C. Bacillus thuringiensisIII. Butterfly caterpillars
D. NucleopolyhedrovirusIV. Aphids

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Target of Ladybird beetle
The beetle with red and black markings, commonly called the Ladybird, is an effective natural predator that feeds on and eliminates aphids.

Step 2: Target of Dragonflies
Dragonflies are predatory insects widely recognized for preying upon and controlling mosquito populations.

Step 3: Target of Bacillus thuringiensis
Spores of Bacillus thuringiensis produce endotoxins that selectively kill butterfly caterpillars when ingested by larvae on vulnerable plants.

Step 4: Role of Nucleopolyhedrovirus
Viruses in the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus (baculoviruses) are biological control agents utilized for species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal control of arthropods without adversely affecting non-target insects, mammals, birds, or plants.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Matching each biocontrol agent with its target or pest control characteristic gives: Ladybird beetle with aphids, Dragonflies with mosquitoes, Bacillus thuringiensis with butterfly caterpillars, and Nucleopolyhedrovirus with species-specific narrow-spectrum insecticidal activity. Therefore, the correct combination is A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q06 - Matching biofertilisers with their specific biological functions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Biofertiliser Organism) List II (Biological Role / Mechanism)
A. RhizobiumI. Free-living nitrogen fixer in the soil
B. GlomusII. Symbiotic fungus absorbing phosphorus for the plant
C. AzotobacterIII. Symbiotic nitrogen fixation in leguminous root nodules
D. AnabaenaIV. Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium serving as biofertiliser in paddy fields

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Rhizobium
Rhizobium forms a symbiotic association within the root nodules of leguminous plants, fixing atmospheric dinitrogen into organic forms that serve as nutrients for the host.

Step 2: Role of Glomus
Species of the genus Glomus form mycorrhizal associations with plant roots, where the fungal symbiont absorbs phosphorus from the soil and transfers it to the plant.

Step 3: Role of Azotobacter
Azotobacter is a free-living bacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen directly in the soil, thereby enriching the soil nitrogen pool without establishing an obligate symbiotic relationship.

Step 4: Role of Anabaena
Anabaena is an autotrophic cyanobacterium capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen, acting as a crucial biofertiliser in waterlogged paddy fields.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Correlating each organism with its specific functional role establishes: Rhizobium with symbiotic nitrogen fixation in legume nodules, Glomus with mycorrhizal phosphorus absorption, Azotobacter with free-living soil nitrogen fixation, and Anabaena with cyanobacterial nitrogen fixation in paddy fields. Consequently, the correct sequence is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q07 - Matching sewage treatment stages with characteristic processes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Treatment Stage / Fraction) List II (Characteristic Process / Feature)
A. Primary treatmentI. Aerobic microbial flocs consume organic matter and reduce BOD
B. Aeration tank activityII. Physical removal of debris and grit via sequential filtration and sedimentation
C. Anaerobic sludge digesterIII. Anaerobic digestion producing methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide
D. Activated sludge settlingIV. Sedimentation of flocs where a small portion is recycled as inoculum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Process of Primary treatment
Primary treatment involves purely physical processes where floating debris is removed by sequential filtration and grit (soil and small pebbles) is removed by gravity sedimentation.

Step 2: Process in the Aeration tank
In aeration tanks, mechanical agitation and constant pumping of air promote vigorous aerobic microbial growth into flocs, which metabolize organic matter and significantly reduce biochemical oxygen demand (BOD).

Step 3: Process in Anaerobic sludge digesters
In anaerobic sludge digesters, anaerobic bacteria digest the bacterial and fungal biomass present in sludge, producing biogas consisting of methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide.

Step 4: Fate of Activated sludge
In settling tanks, bacterial flocs sediment to form activated sludge; a small portion of this sediment is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum, while the remainder undergoes anaerobic digestion.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Matching each stage of sewage treatment with its hallmark mechanism reveals: Primary treatment involves physical filtration and grit sedimentation, Aeration tank activity involves aerobic flocs reducing BOD, Anaerobic sludge digester involves anaerobic digestion generating biogas, and Activated sludge settling involves sediment formation where part returns as inoculum. Hence, the correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q08 - Matching pathogenic microbes and prions with characteristics

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Infectious Agent / Pathogen) List II (Structural / Pathological Feature)
A. AdenovirusI. Proteinaceous infectious agent lacking nucleic acid
B. NucleopolyhedrovirusII. Arthropod pathogen with species-specific, narrow-spectrum activity
C. BacteriophageIII. Virus exhibiting structural head, collar, tail, base plate, and prongs
D. PrionsIV. Virus responsible for respiratory infections in humans

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characteristics of Adenovirus
Adenoviruses are viruses that cause respiratory infections in human beings.

Step 2: Characteristics of Nucleopolyhedrovirus
Baculoviruses belonging to the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus attack insects and other arthropods, displaying species-specific and narrow-spectrum insecticidal activity with no negative impacts on non-target species.

Step 3: Characteristics of Bacteriophage
A bacteriophage is a bacterial virus characterized structurally by an icosahedral head, collar, sheath tail, base plate, pins, and prongs.

Step 4: Characteristics of Prions
Prions are proteinaceous infectious agents that lack any nucleic acid genome and cause transmissible neurological disorders.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Connecting each biological agent with its structural or pathological attribute yields: Adenovirus causes respiratory infections, Nucleopolyhedrovirus provides species-specific arthropod control, Bacteriophage exhibits the head-collar-tail-plate morphology, and Prions represent proteinaceous infectious agents. Hence, the correct combination is A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q09 - Matching water samples with biochemical oxygen demand

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Water Sample / Sludge Fraction) List II (Biochemical / Physical Characteristic)
A. Untreated municipal sewageI. Lowest BOD value indicating minimal biodegradable organic content
B. Secondary treated sewage effluentII. Highest BOD value reflecting intense organic load and high oxygen demand
C. Relatively clean river waterIII. Solid sediment collected solely by physical sedimentation without aeration
D. Primary sludge sedimentIV. Substantially reduced BOD value following aerobic microbial digestion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: BOD profile of Untreated municipal sewage
Untreated municipal sewage carries a massive concentration of biodegradable organic wastes and human excreta, conferring the highest biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) and maximum polluting potential.

Step 2: BOD profile of Secondary treated sewage effluent
Secondary effluent has been subjected to biological oxidation by aerobic flocs in aeration tanks, causing its BOD to be reduced substantially before discharge into natural bodies of water.

Step 3: BOD profile of Clean river water
Natural, unpolluted river water contains negligible concentrations of decomposing organic impurities, thereby exhibiting the lowest BOD value among the water samples.

Step 4: Nature of Primary sludge sediment
Primary sludge consists of all solid particulate matter and grit that settle mechanically at the bottom of the settling basin during primary treatment, before any biological aeration occurs.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Evaluating each sample in terms of organic load and processing state gives: Untreated municipal sewage matches the highest BOD value, Secondary treated effluent matches substantially reduced BOD after microbial oxidation, Clean river water matches the lowest BOD value, and Primary sludge matches the solid sediment collected solely through physical sedimentation. Consequently, the correct sequence is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MATCHING_Q10 - Matching biofertiliser organisms with soil enrichment mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Biofertiliser Organism) List II (Physiological / Ecological Contribution)
A. GlomusI. Mycorrhizal fungus absorbing phosphorus and conferring pathogen and drought resistance
B. RhizobiumII. Symbiotic bacterium converting dinitrogen to organic nutrients within legume root nodules
C. AzospirillumIII. Free-living diazotroph enriching soil nitrogen content without forming root nodules
D. NostocIV. Photosynthetic cyanobacterium fixing nitrogen and adding organic matter to wetland soil

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of Glomus
Members of the genus Glomus establish mycorrhizal associations with plant roots, absorbing phosphorus from the soil while providing benefits such as resistance to root-borne pathogens and tolerance to drought and salinity.

Step 2: Mechanism of Rhizobium
Rhizobium enters an endosymbiotic relationship with leguminous roots, developing specialized nodules where it reduces atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms utilized by the host plant.

Step 3: Mechanism of Azospirillum
Azospirillum is an asymbiotic, free-living bacterium that independently fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the rhizosphere soil, thereby increasing soil nitrogen reserves.

Step 4: Mechanism of Nostoc
Nostoc is an autotrophic, photosynthetic cyanobacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen and contributes substantial organic matter to paddy soils, enhancing overall fertility.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Aligning each biofertiliser with its distinctive physiological adaptation reveals: Glomus acts as a phosphorus-absorbing mycorrhizal partner conferring pathogen and drought resistance, Rhizobium acts as a nodule-forming symbiotic nitrogen fixer, Azospirillum acts as a free-living soil nitrogen fixer, and Nostoc acts as an autotrophic nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium adding organic matter. Thus, the correct sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.
